Open a dataset as a lazy query

Source: R/query.R
store_open.Rd

Builds a lazy query on one dataset of a store, from the files its catalog names (the folder is never listed). The query is transformed with the dplyr verbs filter(), select(), mutate(), rename(), arrange(), distinct(), head(), and run with collect() (an R data frame), compute() (rows kept in memory as Arrow data), pull() or glimpse(). Arrow pushes filters and column selection into the scan, so only the needed files, row groups and columns are read.

Usage

store_open(st, dataset, version = NULL)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect().

dataset

Name of the dataset: the full name, or its last part when that is unique in the store.

version

NULL for the current version, or the 16 hex characters of an earlier version kept in the history (see store_history()).

Value

A lazy query of class rcs_query. Print it to see the dataset, the files left after pruning and the columns.

Details

  • A filter whose columns are all partition columns is first evaluated on the partition values recorded in the catalog: only the files of the matching partitions are opened.

  • store_intersects() adds a spatial filter.

  • collect() returns a tibble, or an sf object for a geospatial dataset whose geometry is read, with the catalog's coordinate reference system. It restores the R types Arrow does not restore by itself (difftime units, bit64::integer64, factor levels, plain list columns) and drops the row identifier .rcs_id that the package adds to geospatial data; the columns h3, bbox and h3_p<r> are returned.

The query reads from the location chosen as for store_read(), with the catalogs held by the connection.

See also

store_read(), store_intersects().

Examples

location <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-open")
st <- store_connect(location, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(500), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 500 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  C:/Users/EB2/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmp6hCb4K/rcs-example-open  2/2
#>   files sent  38.1 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
q <- store_open(st, "daily")
q
#> <rcs_query> sales/daily (table, current)
#> Location: primary
#> Files:    2 of 2
#> Columns:  shop_id, date, year, product, qty, price, promo, grade, delivered, big, wait, note, tags, ts, ts_local
q |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2024, qty > 40) |>
  dplyr::select(shop_id, date, qty) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 43 × 3
#>    shop_id date         qty
#>      <int> <date>     <int>
#>  1       1 2024-12-24    43
#>  2       2 2024-12-17    43
#>  3       3 2024-01-03    45
#>  4       4 2024-06-14    43
#>  5       4 2024-06-17    48
#>  6       4 2024-09-16    47
#>  7       4 2024-11-26    49
#>  8       5 2024-06-09    45
#>  9       6 2024-02-21    43
#> 10       9 2024-02-28    41
#> # ℹ 33 more rows
unlink(location, recursive = TRUE)
